thread:
maria: Heads up — after the AZ routing change at 04:12 UTC we’re seeing a bad GPU skew. 3/12 GPU nodes in us-west1-b are saturated (~95%) and the rest are idling ~10–20%. Customers on Dedicated are seeing latency spikes.

devin: Ugh. I noticed higher eviction churn on pods with affinity to gpu=high. Grafana shows steady queue on the saturated nodes.

samir: grabbing scheduler logs now. Kube-scheduler prints a lot of "failed predicate: PodAffinityRules" around 04:13. suspect topologySpread/affinity swinging after label reconciliation.

jules: We rolled a small AZ routing tweak that changes preferred-locality for allocation. Might have made the scheduler prefer local AZ more aggressively. Could explain packing bias.

kai: Also seeing node re-registrations for a subset of nodes during the same window — kubelet briefly went NotReady (~10s) then back. That can make scheduler treat them as newly available and pack pods there.

maria: Repro steps to inspect noisy nodes:

```bash
kubectl get nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-az=us-west1-b -o wide
kubectl top node $(kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o name | head -n3)
kubectl get pods -o wide -n inference | grep GPU
```

devin: quick check: some pods have nodeAffinity: preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution to prefer same-shard. Combined with aggressive local preference -> hotspot.

samir: Paste from kube-scheduler log (04:13):

```text
I0404 04:13:21.123 scheduler_predicates.go:234] Pod "training-job-7" failed to fit: topologySpreadConstraints violated: [maxSkew:1 topologyKey:kubernetes.io/zone when unschedulable]
I0404 04:13:21.124 scheduler_predicates.go:299] PreferredAffinity matched 8/10 but rejected due to tie-break
```

jules: Two root contributors likely: (1) affinity/topologySpread constraints tuned for strong locality and (2) AZ routing tweak that pushes traffic/allocations into specific AZs.

kai: Network flaps caused some nodes to re-register — that can temporarily drop their labels (we've seen label reapply jobs kicking in). If labels are missing briefly, scheduler may view them as better fit afterwards and pack there.

maria: Impact: elevated preemptions / evictions on multi-tenant nodes, higher tail latency for generation requests, and cost inefficiency (bursting hot nodes while others idle).

devin: Mitigation ideas (quick):
- revert AZ routing change (fast rollback)
- add a short descheduler policy (LowNodeUtilization) to spread pods while we validate
- temporarily relax preferredDuringScheduling to avoid overfitting

samir: I can push a descheduler job: policy snippet I plan to apply:

```json
{"strategy":"LowNodeUtilization","params":{"thresholds":{"cpu":20,"gpu":30},"targetUtilizationPercent":60}}
```

jules: We should avoid immediate aggressive evictions that violate PDBs. Descheduler can respect PDB by default, but confirm. Ops-bot, any constraints?

ops-bot: descheduler-template v2 will respect PodDisruptionBudgets if run with --evict-local-storage=false and eviction-filter configured. Current cluster image has v1.8 deployed in us-west1. Rolling update may be needed.

kai: Short term I recommend: revert routing tweak (devin), deploy descheduler low-util in dry-run for 10m, then enable eviction for non-PDB pods. Also mark a few nodes as buffer (label gpu-buffer=true) and cordon them for test.

devin: I'm starting rollback now. ETA 12m.

samir: I'll prepare the descheduler policy and run in dry-run. Watchlist: eviction events, kube-scheduler logs, node re-registers.

maria: While that runs, we should add a medium-term fix: add topologySpreadConstraints on critical workloads to prefer even distribution across gpu-cohort label instead of strict az locality. And add a node label "gpu-cohort" assigned by provisioner so scheduler has a coarser bucketing.

jules: Agree. Suggest plan: 1) short rollback + descheduler (now). 2) change critical deployment manifests to include:

```yaml
topologySpreadConstraints:
  - maxSkew: 1
    topologyKey: gpu-cohort
    whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
    labelSelector: {matchLabels: {app: inference}}
```

and 3) create automated labelling job in provisioning pipeline.

kai: We'll also add an alert for "GPU imbalance" in Grafana: if stddev of GPU utilization across cohort > 30% for 3 mins, page eng-platform.

devin: Rollback applied at 04:25 UTC. Starting verification.

samir: Descheduler dry-run in place. No evictions yet. Watching target nodes for reallocations.

maria: Early signs: GPU utilization flattening on a couple of hotspots. Evictions dropped from 18/min -> 3/min. Still watching for churn.

jules: Cost note: if this keeps up we'll have >10% wasted paid-GPU time due to imbalanced packing. Need cohort labels to tighten binpacking and allow better defrag.

devin: I'll own the rollback ticket and watch for re-occurrence. samir/jules own descheduler + manifest updates. kai will handle monitoring+alerting. Plan to meet in 30m if skew not resolved.

maria: Thanks all. If anyone sees a customer impact spike, ping #support immediately. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0421.chan-eng-platform. Assigned: devin.

samir: quick follow-up — after descheduler run we should run a simulated binpack job to measure fragmentation index (we have a small tool in infra-utils). I'll kick that once descheduler finishes.

maria: Perfect. Keep updates here.

devin: update @04:36 UTC: rollback steady, GPU skew reduced to ~12% stddev. Leaving descheduler in passive mode for 15 more minutes.

jules: noted. I'll draft the gpu-cohort label plan and a changelog for provisioning.

kai: Alert rule pushed, dashboard updated.

maria: Closing actionables: rollback done, descheduler passive -> scheduled to run for smoothing, manifest changes next 48h. Will reconvene if trend reappears.

devin: closing here. thx everyone.
thread_summary: Root: Maria reports GPU skew after AZ routing tweak. Team diagnoses scheduler affinity + node re-registration flaps as causes. Short-term rollback + descheduler dry-run applied. Medium-term: add gpu-cohort labels and topologySpreadConstraints, update provisioning labeling, add alerting. Owners assigned: devin (rollback), samir (descheduler), jules (manifests), kai (monitoring).
